accuracy.evidence: Checked for using the toilet: the routine and its order match NHS 'How to potty train' (wipe front to back, wash hands after every visit, do not punish accidents) and Development Matters 2021 PSED 3-4 ('using the toilet, washing and drying their hands'); the go-when-you-feel-it rule matches ERIC's advice not to hold on; the flushable list matches Water UK Fine to Flush and the water companies' 3 Ps (pee, poo, paper; wet wipes and paper towels do not break up). The lab accepts flush and pants up in either order because guidance differs, and only fixes what every source agrees on: wipe before pants up, wash after both, dry after wash.

misconceptions.evidence: Each documented slip has its own moment: holding on to finish a game (feeling meter runs into an accident at level 3, challenge tag hold), skipping the wash because hands look clean (Run off to play and early Wash cards are refused, tag germs), pants up before wiping (refused with 'Do not pull them up before you wipe', tag order), wiping back to front (drag the other way is refused, tag wipe), flushing wipes, paper towels or toys (sorted out with pipe-blocking reasons, tag flush), and hiding an accident as naughty (Hide it and Keep wet pants on refused, tag hide).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtoilet is built on this topic's own mechanisms: a body-signal meter that rises with each play and rewards going while the feeling is little, a partial-order step builder where flush and pants up may swap but wash and dry are locked until both are done, a side-view wiping track that reads drag direction (front to back), a flushable or bin sort, and an accident recovery pick. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab, including flagbyebye and flagdress.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each rule by doing: waiting with Keep playing turns the meter red and gives a gentle accident message, so they learn to go at the first feeling; the steps row only accepts a card once its earlier steps are done, so the order is learned from the refusals; the wipe only counts when dragged towards Back; the sort says why wipes block pipes. Done lines confirm in one plain sentence what the child just did.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong answer the lab then disproves: 'Finish the game first' (the meter runs out), 'No, they look clean' (Run off to play is refused until hands are washed and dried), 'Back to front' (a back-to-front drag is refused), 'Yes, it is like paper' for wet wipes (sorted to the bin with the reason), and 'Yes, I am naughty' after an accident (Tell a grown-up and clean pants are the helpers). Each done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions; every wrong option carries a tag with its own message: hold ('Holding on until the game ends can mean an accident'), order ('pants down, sit, wipe, flush, pants up, wash, dry'), germs ('clean-looking hands can still have germs'), wipe ('front to the back'), flush ('Wipes, paper towels and toys block the pipes') and hide ('Accidents are not naughty'). In-step feedback names the slip too, e.g. 'Wipe first, then pants up'.

readability.evidence: Family lesson for ages 3 to 4: kid text uses short sentences and everyday words ('Pants down. Sit on the toilet.'), and passes learn/readability.py; adult text was rewritten into short sentences to pass its limit. Every lab card is a big picture with 1 to 4 words (Wee, Poo, Toilet paper, Hide it), so a child who cannot read can play while a grown-up reads the heading.

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence teaches a step, a reason or a check: kid paragraphs cover the feeling, the order, wiping and washing, and what can be flushed plus accidents; adult paragraphs give the curriculum, the routine and its sources, the common mistakes with their sources, and what each lab step does. No filler phrases (gate clean) and no text repeated from the dressing or goodbye lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light themes and at 1200 px: the 3 feeling cards, the 7-slot steps row with a 3-column card grid, the wipe track with Front (tummy) and Back (bottom) labels, the two sort boxes and the 2-column accident grid all fit with no clipping; cards are at least 100 px wide on a phone, labels shrink to fit and never fall below 11 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every step has HTML buttons as well as canvas taps and drags (Keep playing, Go to the toilet, each step card, Wipe front to back or back to front, Down the toilet or In the bin, each accident card); the canvas aria-label is updated with every message, and the challenge uses buttons with a polite live region. walk.cjs: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, no console errors.

sources: DfE (2021) Development Matters: non-statutory curriculum guidance for the EYFS, PSED, 3 and 4 year olds: 'be increasingly independent in meeting their own care needs, e.g. brushing teeth, using the toilet, washing and drying their hands thoroughly'
DfE (2024) Statutory framework for the early years foundation stage, ELG Managing Self: 'manage their own basic hygiene and personal needs, including dressing, going to the toilet'
NHS (nhs.uk) 'How to potty train': teach girls to wipe from front to back, wash hands, do not punish accidents
ERIC, The Children's Bowel & Bladder Charity (eric.org.uk): go to the toilet when the need is felt; holding on causes accidents and bladder problems
Water UK 'Fine to Flush' standard (2019) and water companies' '3 Ps' (pee, poo, paper) guidance: wet wipes and paper towels do not break down and cause blockages
